title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
authors: Azadeh Alavi, Fatemeh Kouchmeshki, Hossein Akhoundi, Yongli Re, Abdolrahman Alavi, Muhammad Usman
abstract: Recent studies have reported promising results from quantum machine learning in drug discovery, healthcare, materials science and cybersecurity. Research includes comparisons with classical machine learning algorithms and the development of sequential hybrid pipelines. We propose that fusion can improve prediction when classical and quantum representations capture complementary predictive relationships. Our classical-quantum multi-view framework preserves the full classical input alongside simulated quantum features. Concatenation and attention combine the views; single-view comparisons, replacement and masking controls assess both views' contributions. Controlled angular-polynomial experiments distinguish targets adequately represented by a single view from those that depend on complementary angular and polynomial relationships. For these mixed targets, fusion improves prediction by combining the relevant feature sets, while matched classical representations recover the same benefit, linking the improvement to their complementary predictive content. Controlled classification tests further show that gains depend on alignment between the chosen representation and the target, and on a suitable fusion rule. Benchmark validation shows improved mean predictive performance over classical baselines on Wine, Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, three-class Fashion-MNIST and Steel Plates Faults within the evaluated protocols. Classical replacement and masking controls remain competitive, classical baselines lead on Digits and Covertype, and outcomes with missing or corrupted views depend on the available inputs. These findings support evaluating quantum representations for their complementary predictive contribution and matching the representation and fusion strategy to the target relationships.
summary: This paper proposes a multi-view fusion framework to determine when quantum representations enhance classical machine learning predictions. By systematically comparing fusion results against single-view and classical baselines, the authors demonstrate that gains arise specifically when the classical and quantum views capture complementary predictive information. This provides a principled method for assessing the utility of quantum features in practical data analysis.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which combining classical and quantum feature representations (multi-view fusion) improves predictive performance in machine learning tasks.
main_result: Fusion significantly improves prediction when the classical and quantum views capture complementary predictive relationships, which can be confirmed by controlled comparisons against single-view or classical-only baselines.
method: A classical–quantum multi-view framework is employed, combining full classical inputs with features derived from simulated quantum circuits using concatenation or attention mechanisms.
model_or_system: The model involves a hybrid system where classical data is augmented by features extracted from quantum circuits (using qubits, unitary gates, and expectation values as readouts).
key_observables: Mean predictive performance (e.g., Brier loss, F1 score) across various benchmark datasets (Wine, Fashion-MNIST).
important_parameters: The degree of complementarity between the classical and quantum feature sets, and the choice of fusion rule (concatenation vs. attention).
main_assumptions: The improvement is attributed to the complementary predictive content of the views, and the analysis relies on controlled comparisons to isolate this gain.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates various hybrid information flows, including the retained-input multi-view fusion setup. Figure 2 details the single-qubit Bloch sphere geometry and the readout process.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the multi-view framework, details the quantum feature generation process, presents controlled synthetic tasks to diagnose complementarity, validates the approach on multiple ML benchmarks, and concludes by establishing guidelines for when quantum views add value.
why_interesting: While the application is ML, the methodology involves simulating quantum feature extraction and rigorously testing the necessity of quantum information for achieving state-of-the-art predictive power, which touches upon quantum information utility.

(b) This coordinate determines the probabilities of the two Z outcomes and their signed mean. Mixed local states lie inside the sphere. The experiments extend this readout principle to multi-qubit local and pairwise observables.
